name: The skim, rebuilt
note: Sixty-two events for 1279-1947. The skim is deliberately thin, but two eras were running at half an hour of play between authored events, and the COLONIAL class had five of a target thirty. The pre-1300 weighting does not move: the generator asserts it and fails the build if it drifts.

events.title: Paper displaces palm leaf, and the cost of a copy collapses
events.evidence: The shift in surviving manuscript supports, the paper mills recorded at Daulatabad and Kashmir, and the sudden growth in manuscript numbers after this date.
events.note: The single biggest change to the knowledge economy between writing and printing, and nobody fought a battle over it.

events.title: The silver tanka and the copper jital set a currency for the north
events.evidence: The Sultanate mint series, and Barani's account of the market regulations priced in them.

events.title: Muhammad bin Tughlaq issues token currency, and it fails in four years
events.evidence: The brass and copper tokens themselves, and Barani's account of forgery on a scale the state could not police.
events.note: A fiat currency in 1330. The idea was right; the anti-counterfeiting was not.

events.title: Alauddin fixes grain prices and builds the granaries to hold them
events.evidence: Barani's detailed account of the schedule, the state granaries, and the officers who enforced it.

events.title: Ibn Battuta travels India for eight years and writes it down
events.evidence: The Rihla, dictated in Morocco twenty years later, and corroborated in detail by the Sultanate records.

events.title: The Gulf horse trade becomes the Deccan's largest import
events.evidence: The Vijayanagara and Bahmani accounts of purchase contracts, and Marco Polo and Abdur Razzaq on the numbers.
events.note: Horses do not breed well in the Deccan. Every cavalry army in the south was an import bill.

events.title: Zheng He's fleets call at Calicut, Cochin and Bengal
events.evidence: The Chinese voyage records, the Ma Huan account, and the trilingual Galle stele.

events.title: Vijayanagara is founded, by men who had served in Delhi
events.evidence: The Sangama grant series and the Vijayanagara court chronicles, with the disputed account of the founders' conversion and return.

events.title: Jaunpur becomes a court that patronises in its own right
events.evidence: The Sharqi mosque architecture and the sultanate's manuscript patronage record.

events.title: The Gujarat Sultanate and the rise of Ahmedabad
events.evidence: The city's foundation inscription, and the Gujarati and Persian building record.

events.title: Malwa's sultanate builds at Mandu and cooks a book about it
events.evidence: The Ni'matnama, a cookery manuscript illustrated for the Malwa court, and the Mandu building sequence.
events.note: An illustrated recipe book is state records too. It records what a court ate, and who cooked.

events.title: The Sant poets write in the spoken languages and refuse both orthodoxies
events.evidence: The verse of Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev, Dadu and Sena, transmitted in three separate written traditions.

events.title: Bengali literature acquires a court under the Sultanate
events.evidence: The Srikrishnakirtan manuscript, and the Sultanate's patronage of Bengali translations of the Sanskrit epics.
events.note: A Muslim court paid for the first Bengali Mahabharata. The obvious story is the wrong one.

events.title: Vidyapati writes in Maithili and is read across the east
events.evidence: The padavali corpus, and its adoption into the Bengali and Assamese Vaishnava traditions.

events.title: The Deccan famine of the 1330s empties a new capital
events.evidence: Barani and Ibn Battuta, and the Sultanate's own relief measures and their failure.

events.title: Bijapur, Golconda and Ahmadnagar build a Deccan court idiom
events.evidence: The building sequences of the three sultanates, and the Dakhni literary record they patronised.

events.title: The spinning wheel spreads and cotton output multiplies
events.evidence: The earliest Indian depictions and references, and the growth in cotton textile exports that follows.
events.note: A device that multiplies one person's output several times over. It arrives quietly and changes the export economy.

events.title: Sher Shah's rupiya, road and revenue survey
events.evidence: The rupiya itself, still the unit; the Grand Trunk Road's sarais; and the zabt measurement records.
events.note: Five years in power. The currency, the road and the survey all outlast the empire that replaced him.

events.title: The zabt settlement measures land and prices it by a ten-year average
events.evidence: The Ain-i-Akbari's revenue tables, district by district and crop by crop.

events.title: The Ain-i-Akbari records an empire in numbers
events.evidence: The text itself: revenue, prices, wages, army musters, provincial statistics, and the court's own procedures.
events.note: The most detailed statistical account of any pre-modern state anywhere. It is also propaganda. Both are true.

events.title: Akbar's debating hall puts Jesuits, Jains, Zoroastrians and ulema in one room
events.evidence: The Ibadat Khana accounts in the Akbarnama and the Jesuit letters from the mission, which agree about the arguments and not the outcomes.

events.title: Dara Shikoh has fifty Upanishads translated into Persian
events.evidence: The Sirr-i-Akbar manuscript, and the Latin version made from it that reached Schopenhauer.
events.note: A Mughal prince's Persian Upanishads become Europe's first Upanishads, via Latin, in 1801.

events.title: The East India Company is chartered, and the Dutch and French follow
events.evidence: The charters themselves, and the factory records that begin immediately after.

events.title: Indian cotton textiles become the world's largest manufactured export
events.evidence: The Company shipping records, the Dutch VOC accounts, and the English legislation passed to keep the cloth out.
events.note: England banned it. That is how big it was.

events.title: Silver from the Americas flows into India and stays there
events.evidence: The Mughal mint output series, and the European accounts complaining about a trade balance that only went one way.

events.title: Madras, Bombay and Calcutta are founded as company towns
events.evidence: The Company's grants and fort records for Fort St George, the Bombay marriage transfer, and the Sutanuti purchase.

events.title: Shivaji is crowned and a state is built on chauth
events.evidence: The coronation record, the ashta pradhan council, and the revenue documents of the chauth and sardeshmukhi claims.

events.title: The Sikh misls hold the Punjab between empires
events.evidence: The misl records and the coin legends struck in the Gurus' name.

events.title: The Khalsa is instituted at Anandpur
events.evidence: The Sikh chronicles, the hukamnamas, and the immediate change in the community's military organisation.

events.title: The Deccan famine of 1630 kills across three provinces
events.evidence: Peter Mundy's eyewitness account on the road to Surat, the Mughal relief records, and the Dutch factory correspondence.

events.title: The Maunder minimum and a run of failed monsoons
events.evidence: Solar and speleothem records, and the clustering of famine in the Mughal and Deccan archives.

events.title: The imperial atelier makes painting a documented profession
events.evidence: The signed and attributed folios, and the Ain-i-Akbari's list of the leading painters by name.

events.title: Cast artillery and matchlocks change what a fort is for
events.evidence: The surviving guns, the siege accounts, and the change in fortification profile after this date.

events.title: The Taj Mahal is built, and the accounts survive
events.evidence: The building accounts, the craftsmen's wage records, and the completion inscription.
events.note: Late. For ninety-five per cent of this campaign it does not exist, which is why it is not on the map.

events.title: Surat's pilgrim shipping runs on Mughal and Gujarati capital
events.evidence: The port records, the imperial ships Rahimi and Ganj-i-Sawai, and the cartaz passes they had to carry.

events.title: The Satnami rising: peasants and leatherworkers against the empire
events.evidence: The Mughal court accounts of the revolt near Narnaul and its suppression.

events.title: The Banjara carriers move the grain that feeds every army
events.evidence: Mughal and Maratha campaign records of contracted bullock trains, and the European accounts of caravans in the tens of thousands.
events.note: Nobody's subjects, everybody's logistics. An army moved at the speed the Banjaras agreed to.

events.title: The cartaz: the Indian Ocean becomes a licensed sea
events.evidence: The Portuguese pass registers, and the Mughal and Gujarati correspondence about ships stopped for want of one.
events.note: For a thousand years the ocean was open. From here you sail with someone's permission.

events.title: The Goa Inquisition opens and runs for two hundred and fifty years
events.evidence: The Inquisition's own records, and the prohibition of Konkani in public that accompanied it.

events.title: The Company takes the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
events.evidence: The Treaty of Allahabad, and the Company's revenue accounts from the following year.
events.note: The point at which a trading company stops paying for Indian goods with silver and starts paying with Indian taxes.

events.title: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770
events.evidence: The Company's own revenue records, which show collection maintained through the mortality, and the contemporary accounts.
events.note: Revenue collection was held steady while a third of the province died. The records are the Company's own.

events.title: The Permanent Settlement fixes Bengal's revenue for ever
events.evidence: The regulations, and the sale records of estates auctioned for arrears in the decades after.

events.title: Ryotwari and mahalwari: two other ways to make land pay
events.evidence: The Madras and North-Western Provinces settlement reports, and Munro's and Wingate's own accounts of the survey method.

events.title: The Great Trigonometrical Survey measures the subcontinent
events.evidence: The survey's own records, the Everest and Lambton triangulation data, and the Indian computers — Radhanath Sikdar among them — who did the arithmetic.
events.note: The most accurate survey on earth at the time. It was also how you tax and how you move an army.

events.title: Macaulay's Minute settles what language education happens in
events.evidence: The Minute itself, and the English Education Act that followed within months.
events.note: He had read none of the literature he dismissed and said so. The policy stood for a century.

events.title: Railway and telegraph arrive in the same decade
events.evidence: The Bombay-Thane line, the Calcutta-Agra telegraph, and the Company's own case for both as military infrastructure.

events.title: Indian textile manufacturing collapses against Lancashire
events.evidence: The trade series: cloth exports falling and yarn imports rising, and the census occupational data on weavers.

events.title: The indigo system, and the Bengal cultivators who refuse it
events.evidence: The Indigo Commission's evidence, taken from cultivators directly, and Nil Darpan.

events.title: Crown rule replaces the Company
events.evidence: The Government of India Act 1858, and the Queen's Proclamation.

events.title: The decennial census begins to sort the population into categories
events.evidence: The census reports themselves, and the caste enumeration schedules and their revisions.
events.note: Categories written down for administrative convenience hardened into identities. That is a mechanic, not a metaphor.

events.title: Famine kills millions, and then a Famine Code is written
events.evidence: The Famine Commission reports, the mortality estimates, and the export figures for the same years.

events.title: The Archaeological Survey is founded, and the deep past becomes legible
events.evidence: Cunningham's reports, and the excavation record that runs from them to Harappa and Mohenjo-daro in 1921.
events.note: The reason most of this timeline's evidence lines exist. The instrument was colonial; the record is not undone by that.

events.title: The Asiatic Society, and the discovery that the languages are related
events.evidence: The Society's Asiatick Researches, and Jones's 1786 address on Sanskrit, Greek and Latin.

events.title: Printing in the Indian scripts becomes cheap and general
events.evidence: The Serampore press output, the Fort William College texts, and the vernacular newspaper record that follows.
events.note: From here a work can stop being lost. It is the first time that has ever been true.

events.title: Paramountcy: five hundred and sixty-five states that are not sovereign and not provinces
events.evidence: The treaties themselves, the Residency correspondence, and the Chamber of Princes constitution of 1921.
events.note: The game's own title. A sovereignty that exists at somebody else's discretion.

events.title: Indenture carries a million and a half people overseas
events.evidence: The emigration passes, the depot records, and the colonial commissions of inquiry.

events.title: The Indian National Congress meets for the first time
events.evidence: The proceedings of the Bombay session and its seventy-two delegates.

events.title: Bengal is partitioned, and the swadeshi movement answers
events.evidence: The partition order, the boycott records, and the annulment in 1911.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh
events.evidence: The Hunter Committee evidence, including Dyer's own testimony about what he intended.

events.title: The Salt March
events.evidence: The march's daily record, the arrest figures, and the salt law it broke.

events.title: The Government of India Act 1935 becomes most of the future constitution
events.evidence: The Act, and the Constituent Assembly's later adoption of large parts of its structure.

events.title: The Bengal famine of 1943
events.evidence: The Famine Inquiry Commission report, the shipping and procurement records, and the price series.

events.title: Independence, and Partition
events.evidence: The Indian Independence Act, the Radcliffe award, and the refugee and mortality records.
events.note: The campaign ends here. Not on a victory screen — on a boundary drawn in five weeks by a man who had never been to India.
